name: Easy Coleslaw Dressing
headnote: GarlicQueen offers only a line: a creamy dressing built from things already in the cupboard, enough for a 14-ounce bag of slaw mix, usable right away or kept in the fridge. The Allrecipes editors (contributions by Melanie Fincher) expand on why the formula works, explaining that mayonnaise carries the creaminess, sugar balances the acidity of the vinegar and lemon, and the vinegar supplies the tang, with plain salt and pepper being all the seasoning it needs. They note the yield covers about 8 cups of shredded cabbage and carrot, the dressing keeps a week made ahead, and dressed slaw keeps about two days.
comment_digest: The most helpful review (815 votes, raysmom) insists the dressing is right exactly as written and that the point is not to complicate it. The most common addition anyway is celery seed, about a quarter teaspoon; dry mustard, horseradish or Dijon for bite, and a spoonful of buttermilk with honey (307 helpful) are the other frequent tweaks. Half a teaspoon of black pepper reads as a lot, and while a few cut it back, those who followed it report it stays balanced. Sweeteners swap freely - honey, agave, coconut sugar - though one found an artificial sweetener would not emulsify and added crema. Apple cider vinegar is favoured. Making the dressing a day ahead is repeatedly said to improve it, and one salts and rinses the cabbage first to stop the slaw going watery. A recurring gripe: the recipe never says how much cabbage and carrot to use.
flags: One visible review (Jessica, 08/15/2026) describes roasted corn and potatoes baked in an oven and clearly belongs to a different recipe; it was ignored.
